suspicion: '93' in this paper might not be the amine the corpus calls 93.
why_it_looked_real: An IL_name search for '9322' returns 22 corpus rows (A9322_C2'L6 and siblings), which looked like the same catalogue.
the_measurement_that_retired_it: WRONG, AND RETRACTED 2026-11-10 - see R-06. What this cell said was: 'Those are BL_2023-family combinatorial indices with no imidazole.' Both halves are false. The 22 rows are YR_2024, not BL_2023, and 22 of 22 carry a 3-aminopropylimidazole head. The part of R-01 that survives is the substructure search: 173 unique structures over 277 in-vitro rows carry that head, AA_2008 names them 93_O10...93_O18 / 93_N12...93_N18, and KW_2014 names the same structures A93_C12.
verdict: PARTLY RETIRED, PARTLY RETRACTED. The leading token is still not an identity on its own - but the reason recorded here was never measured, and the 22 rows it dismissed were the structure for head 9322. See R-06.

suspicion: The O17O / O17S / O17Se tails might carry a C16 chain, not C14.
why_it_looked_real: SI 1.1 writes '1-Bromotetradecane (6.0 g, 20 mmol)'. 6.0 g / 20 mmol = 300.0 g/mol, which is 1.7 % from 1-bromoHEXAdecane (305.3) and 8.2 % from 1-bromotetradecane (277.3). On that line alone the name and the stoichiometry disagree and the stoichiometry favours C16.
the_measurement_that_retired_it: Two independent lines beat it. (i) The intermediate in the same paragraph: 3.3 g / 12.8 mmol = 257.81 g/mol; 2-(tetradecyloxy)ethanol is 258.45 (0.25 %) and the C16 analogue is 286.50 (10.0 %). (ii) SI 1.2's own bromide line: 5.0 g / 18 mmol = 277.78, which is 0.18 % from 1-bromotetradecane. (iii) The name-token rule: O17 requires 16 chain carbons plus one heteroatom, which C14-alkyl + C2 gives and C16-alkyl + C2 does not.
verdict: RETIRED. C14, and the 6.0 g line is a transcription error by the authors -- logged as C-07.

suspicion: RETRACTION OF MY OWN FINDING. I reported that the 22 corpus rows whose IL_name contains 9322 are 'BL_2023 family, an unrelated index with no imidazole', and on that basis recorded head 9322 as unobtainable - calling it 'the most damaging fact in this curation'.
why_it_looked_real: It did not look real; it was never measured. The claim came from eyeballing the name A9322_C2'L6 in the output of an exploratory grep run before any substructure search, and was then carried forward as though it had been tested. My own leading-token regex required the name to START with 93 or 9322, so a name beginning with A never matched it and those 22 rows went through none of my three keys. A conclusion drawn from a secondary artifact instead of the primary one - the exact pattern REVIEW_PROGRAM.md section 5 was written about.
the_measurement_that_retired_it: (1) CORPUS, re-read directly from data/data_vitro.csv rather than from the reviewer's quote: the 22 rows are Experiment_ID YR_2024, and 22 of 22 match the SMARTS [NX3]CCCn1ccnc1C. Their IL_head_name is A9322 and their IL_head_SMILES is Cc1nccn1CCCN = 1-(3-aminopropyl)-2-METHYLimidazole, the 2-methyl analogue of amine 93. Resolved through corpus_components.smi, which raises on an ambiguous name: A9322 gives one structure across all 22 rows, and 93 (AA_2008, 11 rows) and A93 (KW_2014, 5 rows) give the same single structure NCCCn1ccnc1. (2) THIS PAPER'S OWN FIGURE S1, by axis geometry at 3.93 Da/px: the 9322-O17O base peak measures 765.5 m/z. Predicted [M+H]+ with the 2-methyl head is 764.651, a deviation of +0.8 Da = +0.20 px; with the plain-imidazole head 93 it is 750.635, +14.9 Da = +3.78 px. The panel picks the 2-methyl head by an 18.9x margin on a one-CH2 difference. The same measurement decides between the three glyph candidates the first pass could not separate: 764.73 at 0.20 px, 784.73 at 4.89 px, 794.75 at 7.44 px.
verdict: RETRACTED. Head 9322 = 1-(3-aminopropyl)-2-methylimidazole, corpus-attested and mass-confirmed in this paper. 03_enumerated.csv goes 5 -> 10 lipidoids, a second C10 anchor exists, and the four Figure S3 values for 9322-O17S now have a molecule. The lesson is this project's own standing rule applied to myself: treat a finding as a claim, and measure it before reporting it.
